To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) our method outperformed previous localization methods on the challenging long-term localization benchmark by a large margin and (2) our method is able to explicitly capture and model the capturing conditions, allowing it to be more robust to appearance changes than other methods.

(a) the performance of visual localization methods can be improved by using condition-specific representations, (b) the use of condition-specific representations can be implemented in a simple way, by using a single network with a condition-dependent branch, (c) the use of a condition-specific representation does not require the use of a large dataset of training images, and (d) the use of the proposed condition-specific representation improves the localization performance by a large factor, especially in case of large changes in the capturing conditions

1) the use of global image descriptors allows the retrieval-based approach to outperform the traditional feature-based approach in terms of accuracy; 2) our condition-based representations, which are computed by condition-specific sub-network, are very effective in handling day-night variation; 3) our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art in long-term localization, especially when day-night variation is present in the test data.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of long-term localization from images is not a matter of feature quality, but rather a question of representation efficiency.
the retrieval-based paradigm is very flexible, and can be adapted to handle challenging variations in appearance.
the use of a retrieval-based approach, combined with a condition-specific representation, is a promising direction to improve localization performance in case of strong appearance variations.
